reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the only convenience right (§ 6(a)) is available solely when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so on an evergreen term (§ 2) the Customer has no convenience exit from an active engagement — this fails the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right on 30–90 days' notice without material penalty.

The redline is additive and minimal: a new § 6(c) granting Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, with payment for Services performed and refund of prepaid, unearned fees, tracking the model language without disturbing the existing breach and mutual-termination provisions.

Leaving the Vendor side untouched is defensible and consistent with the rule: Contractor's 15-day right under § 6(a) likewise operates only when no SOW is outstanding, so it is not a mid-term walk-away right; this is noted accurately in the rationale.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a phrasing artifact — the inserted text uses the contract's defined term 'Company' (a Customer alias) rather than 'Customer', and substantively delivers the required right, notice period and refund.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, explains the gap and the change, and offers the 60-day fallback as the playbook contemplates.
